Summary of National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993
Objective:
The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis Act, 1993, aims to establish a national body overseeing the welfare and socio-economic development of Safai Karamcharis, individuals engaged in manual sanitation work.
Key Provisions:
1.	Commission Setup
•	Constitution: Established by the Central Government.
•	Membership: Includes a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson, and five Members, with a mandatory female representation.
2.	Operational Framework
•	Term of Office: Members serve for a specified period, with conditions for early termination or completion.
•	Resignation and Removal: Defined processes for leaving office or being removed.
3.	Core Responsibilities
•	Functions:
1.	Policy Recommendations: For eliminating inequalities among Safai Karamcharis.
2.	Scheme Evaluation: Improving rehabilitation programs.
3.	Grievance Redressal: Investigating unmet needs or grievances.
4.	Reporting: Submitting periodic reports to Central and State Governments.
•	Authorities:
•	Power to solicit information from governmental authorities for effective functioning.
4.	Administrative Provisions
•	Public Servant Status: Extended to Commission members and staff.
•	Consultative Role: Mandatory consultation with the Commission by the Central Government on policy matters.
•	Transparency and Accountability:
•	Annual Reporting: Submission to the Central Government and subsequent presentation to Parliament.
•	Delegation of Powers and Protection from Liability for actions taken in good faith.

indexableObject.name: Right to compel to any act of duty.

dc.identifier.section_page_note.value:
The beneficiary has a right that his trustee shall be compelled to perform any particular act of his duty as such, and restrained from committing any contemplated or probable breach of trust.
Illustrations
(a) A contracts with B to pay him monthly Rs.100 for the benefit of C. B writes and signs a letter declaring that he will hold in trust for C the money so to be paid. A fails to pay the money in accordance with his contract. C may compel B on a proper indemnity to allow C to sue on the contract in B's name.
(b) A is trustee of certain land, with a power to sell the same and pay the proceeds to B and C equally. A is about to make an improvident sale of the land. B may sue on behalf of himself and C for an injunction to restrain A from making the sale.
